messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [P1] GPU pool eu-west-1-large saturated; queue_depth=12,300; autoscaler returned error 'scaleup_throttled: reached max_nodes (20)'. Public inference API 503s trend rising. See dashboard: https://internal.redwood/ops/metrics/1898765432

oncall-tilly: I'm on it. Paging dmitri and mira. Any quick check on which workloads are the hot ones? Hosted or Dedicated?

dmitri.k: Hosted traffic spike from AcmeChat and a couple of eval jobs from internal CI. Looks like the autoscaler couldn't request more instances — hitting the customer max_nodes cap in config.

mira.s: Confirmed: controller logs show repeated failures: 
```
ERROR autoscaler-controller: scale request denied: "exceeded max_nodes=20"
request: +8 nodes
timestamp: 2026-03-15T09:12:33Z
stack: controller/scale.go:142
```

lex: Queue backlog shows continuous growth on the gpu-encoder queue. Prefix cache misses high so warmup cost is spiking provisioning time.

oncall-tilly: Ok mitigation plan — manual scale to buy time, eject low-priority jobs, bump allowed max_nodes in config, restart controller to pick up config. Who can run the manual scale?

karthik: I can run manual scale now. Running: `k-scale pool eu-west-1-large --replicas 28`

support-bot: Notifying customer-success of impacted tenants: AcmeChat, FinBot, and internal-evals.

customer-success: Reached out to AcmeChat and FinBot with a brief note; they reported increased latency and some 503s since 09:08 UTC. No data loss.

mira.s: Patch to cluster config to raise max_nodes to 30 (applied to staging then prod): 
```bash
kubectl patch configmap autoscaler-config -n infra --patch '{"data":{"max_nodes":"30"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/autoscaler-controller -n infra
```

oncall-tilly: After manual scale and config patch, queue depth starting to decline. Visible metrics: queue_depth -> 12.3k -> 6.1k in ~6m.

dmitri.k: Adding eviction of low-priority batch jobs: `kubectl label job team=batch priority=low && k-evict --label priority=low` — cleared ~1.8k backlog.

incident-bot: Auto-alert: scale event successful. New node_count=28, controller health=OK.

lex: Observed tail latency for hosted gen endpoints peaked at ~4.2s during the hottest window, now trending back toward baseline ~230ms.

oncall-tilly: Summarizing mitigation timeline for handoff: 
- 09:08 UTC: incident-bot alerted on pool saturation and autoscaler error.
- 09:11 UTC: manual scale to 28 requested by karthik.
- 09:14 UTC: config max_nodes bumped to 30 and controller restarted (mira).
- 09:20 UTC: eviction of low-priority jobs cleared ~1.8k queue entries (dmitri).
- 09:24 UTC: queue depth under control, tail latency reducing.

karthik: Logs around restart: 
```
INFO autoscaler-controller: reloading config, new max_nodes=30
INFO autoscaler-controller: reconcile loop succeeded, scaled to 28
```

customer-success: Customers updated: AcmeChat acknowledged; FinBot on standby but OK for now. Shared ETA for full stabilization ~20 minutes.

oncall-tilly: Current status: mitigated -> monitoring. No active alerts if queue < 2k for 10m. I'm handing off to next-oncall-jun for 09:45–12:45 UTC window. See action items below.

next-oncall-jun: Acked. I'll monitor the queue and watch for any churn in provisioning.

mira.s: Immediate action items (assigned inline): 
- [dmitri.k] root cause analysis + postmortem draft (due EOD tomorrow).
- [platform] increase default max_nodes for eu-west-1-large from 20 -> 35 and add an operational guardrail.
- [sre] add alert: sustained "scaleup_throttled" for >3m and queue_depth >5k (severity P1).
- [devex] document fallback guidance for partners to avoid long-running eval floods (owner: lex).

dmitri.k: Initial RCA notes: autoscaler hit configured max_nodes (policy limit) during an unexpected traffic correlated with cache-miss heavy workloads. Two contributing factors: (1) aggressive CI evals running in hosted while ramp, (2) conservative default max_nodes for that pool.

oncall-tilly: Impact summary for postmortem: ~16 minutes of elevated 503s and latency spikes for hosted API; dedicated customers on reserved capacity unaffected except for queued on-demand batches. No data loss; customers were notified.

next-oncall-jun: I'll take on follow ups for the alert and watch the rollout for the default max_nodes bump. If anything regresses I'll page SRE.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> monitoring -> resolved (mitigated).

mira.s: Thanks all — will sync up with product and customer success for the postmortem notes. 

oncall-tilly: Closing notes: keep CI evals rate-limited during peak hours and set quota for internal jobs so they don't trample autoscaler headroom. :thumbsup:
